function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity was discovered and studied by many scientists over centuries. Early observations of static electricity date back to ancient Greek philosophers such as Thales of Miletus (circa 600 BCE). Modern scientific investigation began in the 17th and 18th centuries with figures like William Gilbert, who coined the term “electricity,” and Benjamin Franklin, who conducted famous kite experiments. Subsequent breakthroughs came from Alessandro Volta, who invented the voltaic pile (the first battery), and others such as Luigi Galvani and Michael Faraday, who laid the foundations for electromagnetism.
